q: (only Allaah knows the meaning of these letters).
v.s: Kāf, Hā, Yā, ‘Ayn, Sād.
v.c: Kãf-Ha-Ya-’Aĩn- Ṣãd.

q: Mention of the mercy of your Rabb towards His slave
v.s: [This is] a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zechariah
v.c: ˹This is˺ a reminder of your Lord’s mercy to His servant Zachariah,

v.s: When he called to his Lord a private call [i.e., supplication].
v.c: when he cried out to his Lord privately,

q: “O my Rabb! My bones have weakened
and my hair has turned white because of old age. I have never
(I therefore have great hope that this du'aa will also be accepted).'
v.s: He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled with white, and never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy [i.e., disappointed].
v.c: saying, “My Lord! Surely my bones have become brittle, and grey hair has spread across my head, but I have never been disappointed in my prayer to You, my Lord!

q: “I fear for my relatives after me
(I fear that they may forsake the Deen after I die).
(a son to help me in propagating the Deen)...”
v.s: And indeed, I fear the successors after me, and my wife has been barren, so give me from Yourself an heir
v.c: And I am concerned about ˹the faith of˺ my relatives after me, since my wife is barren. So grant me, by Your grace, an heir,

q: from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qoob
(so that he can guide my people if they stray from their Deen).
And, O my Rabb, make him beloved unto You
(by making him a person who practises the knowledge of Deen that he possesses).'
v.s: Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, pleasing [to You]."
v.c: who will inherit ˹prophethood˺ from me and the family of Jacob, and make him, O Lord, pleasing ˹to You˺!”

q: (In reply to his du'aa, Allaah sent an angel to him who said,)
“O Zakariyya, We convey to you the good news of
a son called Yahya. We have never named anyone like this before him.”
(His name and his character were unique.)
v.s: [He was told], "O Zechariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. We have not assigned to any before [this] name."
v.c: ˹The angels announced,˺ “O Zachariah! Indeed, We give you the good news of ˹the birth of˺ a son, whose name will be John—a name We have not given to anyone before.”

q: said, “O my Rabb! How will I have a son when my wife is barren
(unable to bear children at the age of 98)
and I have reached the pinnacle of old age
v.s: He said, "My Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife has been barren and I have reached extreme old age?"
v.c: He wondered, “My Lord! How can I have a son when my wife is barren, and I have become extremely old?”

q: (what Allaah wills will come to pass even though it seems astonishing).
Your Rabb declares 'It will be easy for Me. Indeed I have created you before whereas you were nothing
(in a like manner, I can create anything even though the means are unavailable.)'”
v.s: [An angel] said, "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, for I created you before, while you were nothing.'"
v.c: An angel replied, “So will it be! Your Lord says, ‘It is easy for Me, just as I created you before, when you were nothing!’”

q: said, “O my Rabb! Appoint a sign for me
(by which I may know that my wife has conceived).”
He said, “Your sign shall be that you will be unable to speak to people for three nights, even though you will be healthy
(your inability to speak will not be because of any disease).”
v.s: [Zechariah] said, "My Lord, make for me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, [being] sound."
v.c: Zachariah said, “My Lord! Grant me a sign.” He responded, “Your sign is that you will not ˹be able to˺ speak to people for three nights, despite being healthy.”

q: came to his people from the sanctuary
(the place where he engaged in Ibaadah)
gestured to them, “Engage in glorifying your Rabb morning and evening
(as you normally do. However, additional thanks will now have to be expressed to Allaah because of the successor to be born).”
v.s: So he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and signaled to them to exalt [God] in the morning and afternoon.
v.c: So he came out to his people from the sanctuary, signalling to them to glorify ˹Allah˺ morning and evening.

q: (Subsequently, Yahya ﵊ was born. When he came of age, Allaah commanded him saying,)
O Yahya! Hold fast on to the scripture
(diligently practise the injunctions of the Torah).”
v.s: [God said], "O John, take the Scripture [i.e., adhere to it] with determination." And We gave him judgement [while yet] a boy
v.c: ˹It was later said,˺ “O John! Hold firmly to the Scriptures.” And We granted him wisdom while ˹he was still˺ a child,

q: (because of which he never committed any sins).
v.s: And affection from Us and purity, and he was fearing of God
v.c: as well as purity and compassion from Us. And he was God-fearing,

q: He was kind to his parents and was neither rebellious
v.s: And dutiful to his parents, and he was not a disobedient tyrant.
v.c: and kind to his parents. He was neither arrogant nor disobedient.

q: Peace be on him on the day he was born on the day that he passed away and on the day when he will be resurrected.
(May he enjoy peace on all these days which is the most traumatic in a persons life.)
v.s: And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.
v.c: Peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day of his death, and the day he will be raised back to life!

q: When she drew away from her family to go to a place far to the east
v.s: And mention, [O Muhammad], in the Book [the story of] Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east.
v.c: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Mary when she withdrew from her family to a place in the east,

m: then he assumed for her the likeness
then he assumed for her the likeness
q: to her, who assumed the appearance of a perfect man before her.
v.s: And she took, in seclusion from them, a screen. Then We sent to her Our Angel [i.e., Gabriel], and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man.
v.c: screening herself off from them. Then We sent to her Our angel, ˹Gabriel,˺ appearing before her as a man, perfectly formed.

q: She said, “I seek Ar Rahmaan's protection from you, if you fear
(If you fear Allaah, you would leave me in peace because He will punish you for harming me).'
v.s: She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, [so leave me], if you should be fearing of God."
v.c: She appealed, “I truly seek refuge in the Most Compassionate from you! ˹So leave me alone˺ if you are God-fearing.”

q: said, “I am but a messenger of your Rabb
to convey to you the good news of a pure son
(that is to be born to you).”
v.s: He said, "I am only the messenger of your Lord to give you [news of] a pure boy [i.e., son]."
v.c: He responded, “I am only a messenger from your Lord, ˹sent˺ to bless you with a pure son.”

q: She responded, “How can I have a son when no man has touched me
and I have never been adulterous
(How will I conceive a child when I have never had intimate relations with a man either lawfully or unlawfully)?”
v.s: She said, "How can I have a boy while no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?"
v.c: She wondered, “How can I have a son when no man has ever touched me, nor am I unchaste?”

m: and so that We will make him
q: (the command of your Rabb will come to pass even though the means are not) present).
(giving her a child without a father)
(We intend giving her this child in a miraculous manner)
(by which they can realise Our power)
(towards those who will follow him as their Nabi).
v.s: He said, "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign to the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed.'"
v.c: He replied, “So will it be! Your Lord says, ‘It is easy for Me. And so will We make him a sign for humanity and a mercy from Us.’ It is a matter ˹already˺ decreed.”

q: (when it was time to deliver the child, she)
withdrew with him to a distant place.
(She travelled approximately 8km from home to Baytul Lahm [Bethlehem], fearing the people's angry reaction to her pregnancy without being married.)
v.s: So she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a remote place.
v.c: So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place.

q: The labour pains brought her to the trunk of a date palm
She said, “Oh! If only I had died before this and had been completely forgotten
(in that way, I would not have to suffer the difficulty of being here all alone without any provisions and I would not have to worry about the insults of people when they see me with a baby).”
v.s: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten."
v.c: Then the pains of labour drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She cried, “Alas! I wish I had died before this, and was a thing long forgotten!”

q: (from a place where he could not see her)
Your Rabb has created a stream
(so that you can easily have water).'
v.s: But he called her from below her, "Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream.
v.c: So a voice reassured her from below her, “Do not grieve! Your Lord has provided a stream at your feet.

q: “(Allaah has also arranged food. All you need to do is to lightly)
Shake the trunk of the date palm towards you, causing fresh ripened
v.s: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.
v.c: And shake the trunk of this palm tree towards you, it will drop fresh, ripe dates upon you.

q: “So eat, drink and cool your eyes
(be happy with your child and the thought that he will be one of Allaah's chosen servants). (As far as your concern about what to tell people, Allaah will see to that as well. Therefore,)
then say, 'I have vowed to fast for Ar Rahmaan, so I cannot speak to anyone today
(because the fasting during their times entailed not speaking as well as not eating).”
v.s: So eat and drink and be contented. And if you see from among humanity anyone, say, 'Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful abstention, so I will not speak today to [any] man.'"
v.c: So eat and drink, and put your heart at ease. But if you see any of the people, say, ‘I have vowed silence to the Most Compassionate, so I am not talking to anyone today.’”

q: (Taking courage from the words of Jibra'eel ﵊ and after regaining her strength with the dates and water, she decided to return home. Consequently,)
She brought the child before her people. They exclaimed, “O Maryam! You have surely perpetrated a grave
v.s: Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, "O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented.
v.c: Then she returned to her people, carrying him. They said ˹in shock˺, “O Mary! You have certainly done a horrible thing!

q: “O sister of Haaroon! Your father was never an evil
person, neither was your mother adulterous
v.s: O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.”
v.c: O sister of Aaron! Your father was not an indecent man, nor was your mother unchaste.”

q: (Adhering to the instructions of Jibra'eel ﵊, she did not answer and)
(indicating to them that they should speak to the child).
They said, “How can we speak to one who is still a baby in a cradle?”
v.s: So she pointed to him. They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle a child?"
v.c: So she pointed to the baby. They exclaimed, “How can we talk to someone who is an infant in the cradle?”

q: said, “I am a slave of Allaah
(contrary to the beliefs of the Christians who claim that he is Allaah or Allaah's son).
(contrary to the beliefs of the Jews who claim that he was not a Nabi)...”
v.s: [Jesus] said, "Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.
v.c: Jesus declared, “I am truly a servant of Allah. He has destined me to be given the Scripture and to be a prophet.

q: “Allaah has blessed me wherever I may be
(so that I may always be of benefit to people)
and has commanded me to perform salaah and to pay zakaah
(when I return to the world before Qiyaamah)
as long as I remain alive.”
v.s: And He has made me blessed wherever I am and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakāh as long as I remain alive
v.c: He has made me a blessing wherever I go, and bid me to establish prayer and give alms-tax as long as I live,

q: “Allaah has also made me kind to my mother
and has not made me a tyrant
v.s: And [made me] dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant.
v.c: and to be kind to my mother. He has not made me arrogant or defiant.

q: “Peace be on me on the day I was born, on the day death comes to me
(after I return to this world before Qiyaamah),
and the day when I shall be resurrected
(because these are the most traumatic times in a person's life.”
v.s: And peace is on me the day I was born and the day I will die and the day I am raised alive."
v.c: Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I will be raised back to life!”

q: This is Isa the son of Maryam.
(because the Christians claim that Isa ﵊ was Allaah's son).
v.s: That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute.
v.c: That is Jesus, son of Mary. ˹And this is˺ a word of truth, about which they dispute.
v.h: Christians and Jews Differ on Jesus

q: for Allaah to take a son. He is Pure
anything, all He has to say is “Be!” and it comes into being.
v.s: It is not [befitting] for God to take a son; exalted is He! When He decrees an affair, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.
v.c: It is not for Allah to take a son! Glory be to Him. When He decrees a matter, He simply tells it, “Be!” And it is!

q: (Assert your Imaan in Allaah, as Isa ﵊ told the people when He said,)
“Without doubt Allaah is my Rabb and your Rabb
so worship Him. This is the straight path
v.s: [Jesus said], "And indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is a straight path."
v.c: ˹Jesus also declared,˺ “Surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him ˹alone˺. This is the Straight Path.”

q: (some saying that Isa ﵊ is Allaah and others saying that he is one of three gods).
Woe be to the Kuffaar on the occasion of a momentous
(the Day of Qiyaamah when they will be punished for their corrupt beliefs).
v.s: Then the factions differed [concerning Jesus] from among them, so woe to those who disbelieved - from the scene of a tremendous Day.
v.c: Yet their ˹various˺ groups have differed among themselves ˹about him˺, so woe to the disbelievers when they face a tremendous Day!

q: How well will they hear and see on the day when they will come to Us!
(Unlike the condition of the Kuffaar in this world when they fail to see and hear the truth, they will clearly see and hear the truth on the Day of Qiyaamah when it will be too late.)
v.s: How [clearly] they will hear and see the Day they come to Us, but the wrongdoers today are in clear error.
v.c: How clearly will they hear and see on the Day they will come to Us! But today the wrongdoers are clearly astray.

q: Warn them of the day of remorse
(the Day of Qiyaamah when people will regret the wrong they did in this world),
they are negligent and do not want to accept Imaan.
v.s: And warn them, [O Muhammad], of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be concluded; and [yet], they are in [a state of] heedlessness, and they do not believe.
v.c: And warn them ˹O Prophet˺ of the Day of Regret, when all matters will be settled, while they are ˹engrossed˺ in heedlessness and disbelief.

q: Without a shadow of doubt, We will inherit
the earth and whoever is on it
(on the Day of Qiyaamah when all creation will be no more)
(they will go nowhere else and will have to answer to Us).
v.s: Indeed, it is We who will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned.
v.c: Indeed, it is We Who will succeed the earth and whoever is on it. And to Us they will ˹all˺ be returned. Abraham and His Father, Ȃzar

v.s: And mention in the Book [the story of] Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
v.c: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Abraham. He was surely a man of truth and a prophet.

q: “O my father! Why do you worship things
that cannot hear, cannot see and cannot be of any assistance to you?”
v.s: [Mention] when he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and will not benefit you at all?
v.c: ˹Remember˺ when he said to his father, “O dear father! Why do you worship what can neither hear nor see, nor benefit you at all?

q: has come to me that has not come to you, so follow me and I shall show you the straight path
(the path of Towheed that leads to eternal salvation).”
v.s: O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to an even path.
v.c: O dear father! I have certainly received some knowledge which you have not received, so follow me and I will guide you to the Straight Path.

q: (because the object of worship is to please the one being worshipped and worshipping idols pleases only Shaytaan, worshipping idols is equal to worshipping Shaytaan).
Indeed Shaytaan was ever disobedient to Ar Rahmaan
(and therefore deserves no reverence at all).”
v.s: O my father, do not worship [i.e., obey] Satan. Indeed Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient.
v.c: O dear father! Do not worship Satan. Surely Satan is ever rebellious against the Most Compassionate.

q: “O my father! Indeed I fear that
a punishment would afflict you from Ar Rahmaan, after which you would be a friend
v.s: O my father, indeed I fear that there will touch you a punishment from the Most Merciful so you would be to Satan a companion [in Hellfire]."
v.c: O dear father! I truly fear that you will be touched by a torment from the Most Compassionate, and become Satan’s companion ˹in Hell˺.” Ȃzar’s Angry Response

q: my gods, O Ibraheem? If you do not stop
v.s: [His father] said, "Have you no desire for my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so avoid me a prolonged time."
v.c: He threatened, “How dare you reject my idols, O Abraham! If you do not desist, I will certainly stone you ˹to death˺. So be gone from me for a long time!”

q: (Because Ibraheem ﵊ thought that Allaah would still guide his father, he added,)
I shall shortly seek forgiveness from my Rabb on your behalf. He has always been compassionate
v.s: [Abraham] said, "Peace [i.e., safety] will be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord. Indeed, He is ever gracious to me.
v.c: Abraham responded, “Peace be upon you! I will pray to my Lord for your forgiveness. He has truly been Most Gracious to me.

q: which you worship instead of Allaah
(I shall physically separate from you just as I am spiritually separated from you).
(being away from you people and being able to peacefully worship Allaah,)
my Rabb. I am hopeful that I shall not be deprived
v.s: And I will leave you and those you invoke other than God and will invoke my Lord. I expect that I will not be in invocation to my Lord unhappy [i.e., disappointed]."
v.c: As I distance myself from ˹all of˺ you and from whatever you invoke besides Allah, I will ˹continue to˺ call upon my Lord ˹alone˺, trusting that I will never be disappointed in invoking my Lord.”

q: and refrained from what they worshipped instead of Allaah, We gifted him with
Ya'qoob. We made each one of them a Nabi.
v.s: So when he had left them and those they worshipped other than God, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each [of them] We made a prophet.
v.c: So after he had left them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and made each of them a prophet.

q: them a portion of Our mercy
(We made it such that future generations will always praise them).
v.s: And We gave them of Our mercy, and We made for them a mention [i.e., reputation] of high honour.
v.c: We showered them with Our mercy, and blessed them with honourable mention.

q: and was a Rasool, a Nabi.
v.s: And mention in the Book, Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
v.c: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Moses. He was truly a chosen man, and was a messenger and a prophet.

q: We called him from the right side of Mount Toor
(to form ally declare him a Rasool as he returned to Egypt from Madyan)
and We brought him close in communion
v.s: And We called him from the side of the mount at [his] right and brought him near, confiding [to him].
v.c: We called him from the right side of Mount Ṭûr, and drew him near, speaking ˹with him˺ directly.

q: From Our mercy We gifted him with his brother Haaroon as a Nabi.
v.s: And We gave him out of Our mercy his brother Aaron as a prophet.
v.c: And We appointed for him—out of Our grace—his brother, Aaron, as a prophet.

q: Verily he was true to his promise and he was a Rasool, a Nabi.
(This denotes the superiority of Ismaa'eel over Is'haaq, who was only a Nabi and not a Rasool.)
v.s: And mention in the Book, Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
v.c: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Ishmael. He was truly a man of his word, and was a messenger and a prophet.

q: (Besides being steadfast with salaah and Zakaah,)
used to instruct his family to perform salaah and to pay zakaah and he was beloved to his Rabb.
v.s: And he used to enjoin on his people prayer and zakāh and was to his Lord pleasing [i.e., accepted by Him].
v.c: He used to urge his people to pray and give alms-tax. And his Lord was well pleased with him.

v.s: And mention in the Book, Idrees. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
v.c: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Enoch. He was surely a man of truth and a prophet.

q: We elevated him to a high rank
v.s: And We raised him to a high station.
v.c: And We elevated him to an honourable status.

q: (Ambiyaa ﵊ mentioned above from Zakariyya ﵊ until Idrees ﵊)
are the ones whom Allaah has favoured from the progeny of Aadam and from the progeny of those whom We carried with Nooh
(some of them such as Ismaa'eel ﵊ and Is'haaq ﵊ were)
from the progeny of Ibraheem and
(others like Moosa ﵊, Haaroon ﵊, Zakariyya ﵊ and were from the progeny of)
those whom We guided and selected. When the Aayaat of their Rabb are recited, they fall down weeping in prostration.
(It is therefore befitting of anyone who reveres them to behave in the same manner.) (One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah)
v.s: Those were the ones upon whom God bestowed favor from among the prophets of the descendants of Adam and of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel [i.e., Jacob], and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration and weeping.
v.c: Those were ˹some of˺ the prophets who Allah has blessed from among the descendants of Adam, and of those We carried with Noah ˹in the Ark˺, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those We ˹rightly˺ guided and chose. Whenever the revelations of the Most Compassionate were recited to them, they fell down, prostrating and weeping.

q: were followed by such evil successors who destroyed salaah
(by either rejecting the command or by neglecting its performance)
v.s: But there came after them successors [i.e., later generations] who neglected prayer and pursued desires; so they are going to meet evil -
v.c: But they were succeeded by generations who neglected prayer and followed their lusts and so will soon face the evil consequences.

q: and who carries out good acts. These people will enter Jannah and will not be oppressed in the least
(no one will be punished for a sin one did not commit nor deprived of any reward that one deserves).
v.s: Except those who repent, believe and do righteousness; for those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged at all.
v.c: As for those who repent, believe, and do good, it is they who will be admitted into Paradise, never being denied any reward.

q: Theirs shall be eternal Jannaat that Ar Rahmaan has promised His bondsmen in the unseen
Undoubtedly, His promise shall come to pass
(for nothing can prevent it from occurring).
v.s: [Therein are] gardens of perpetual residence which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise has ever been coming.
v.c: ˹They will be in˺ the Gardens of Eternity, promised in trust by the Most Compassionate to His servants. Surely His promise will be fulfilled.

q: they will not hear any futile
(greetings of Salaam and talk that will increase their peace and comfort).
(at all times, as and when they please).
v.s: They will not hear therein any ill speech - only [greetings of] peace - and they will have their provision therein, morning and afternoon.
v.c: There they will never hear any idle talk—only ˹greetings of˺ peace. And there they will have their provisions morning and evening.

q: This is the Jannah that Our bondsmen with Taqwa shall inherit
v.s: That is Paradise, which We give as inheritance to those of Our servants who were fearing of God.
v.c: That is Paradise, which We will grant to whoever is devout among Our servants.

q: (When Rasulullaah ﵊ requested to visit him more often, Allaah instructed Jibra'eel ﵊ to reply by saying,)
only by the command of your Rabb
(we cannot come and go when we please).
(whatever times and places lay ahead of us),
(whatever times and places we have passed by)
and whatever is between the two. Your Rabb never forgets
(and will send to you all the revelation that you are due to receive).”
v.s: [Gabriel said], "And we [angels] descend not except by the order of your Lord. To Him belongs that before us and that behind us and what is in between. And never is your Lord forgetful -
v.c: “We only descend by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs whatever is before us, and whatever is behind us, and everything in between. And your Lord is never forgetful.

q: The Rabb of the heavens, the earth and whatever is between the two, so worship Him and be steadfast in His worship
Do you know of any that
(There is none who has the attributes to be worthy of being called Allaah.)
v.s: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them - so worship Him and have patience for His worship. Do you know of any similarity to Him?"
v.c: ˹He is the˺ Lord of the heavens, and the earth, and everything in between. So worship Him ˹alone˺, and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of anyone equal to Him ˹in His attributes˺?”

q: says, “Shall I be resurrected alive after I have
v.s: And man [i.e., the disbeliever] says, "When I have died, am I going to be brought forth alive?"
v.c: Yet ˹some˺ people ask ˹mockingly˺, “After I die, will I really be raised to life again?”

q: that We created him before when he was nothing?
(In a like manner, We shall create him again after he has died.)
v.s: Does man not remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?
v.c: Do ˹such˺ people not remember that We created them before, when they were nothing?

q: By your Rabb! We will certainly gather them
We shall then present them before Jahannam
v.s: So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils; then We will bring them to be present around Hell upon their knees.
v.c: By your Lord ˹O Prophet˺! We will surely gather them along with the devils, and then set them around Hell on their knees.

q: Then We will definitely separate from every group those who were most rebellious
(so that they can suffer the worst punishment).
v.s: Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were worst against the Most Merciful in insolence.
v.c: Then We will certainly begin by dragging out of every group the ones most defiant to the Most Compassionate.

q: know best who most deserve to enter
v.s: Then, surely it is We who are most knowing of those most worthy of burning therein.
v.c: And We truly know best who is most deserving of burning in it.

q: Every one of you shall pass by it
(everyone shall pass over Jahannam as they cross the bridge of Siraat that spans Jahannam).
(every person will have to pass over the bridge of Siraat. Those headed for Jannah will pass over it speedily and enter Jannah while the others will fall off and land in Jahannam).
v.s: And there is none of you except he will come to it. This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.
v.c: There is none of you who will not pass over it. ˹This is˺ a decree your Lord must fulfil.

q: those with Taqwa and We will leave the oppressors
v.s: Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers within it, on their knees.
v.c: Then We will deliver those who were devout, leaving the wrongdoers there on their knees.

q: When Our clear Aayaat are recited to them
those who commit kufr ask those who have Imaan, “Which of the two groups
standing and which has a finer
(army, group of supporters)?” (Because the Kuffaar have more wealth, larger numbers and greater influence in society, they assume that they are the beloved of Allaah.)
v.s: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Which of [our] two parties is best in position and best in association?"
v.c: When Our clear revelations are recited to them, the disbelievers ask the believers ˹mockingly˺, “Which of the two of us is better in status and superior in assembly?”

q: (Allaah replies to this assumption by telling them,)
How many generations did We destroy before them, who were better off than them in terms of resources and appearance?
(Their great wealth and resources meant nothing to Allaah. Neither were they beloved to Allaah, nor were they saved from His punishment.)
v.s: And how many a generation have We destroyed before them who were better in possessions and [outward] appearance?
v.c: ˹Imagine, O Prophet˺ how many peoples We have destroyed before them, who were far better in luxury and splendour!

q: (Allaah gives a second reply to their assumption by instructing Rasulullaah ﷺ to)
(He will grant them more bounties of this world)
(increase in kufr and sin and eventually)
has been promised to them, which shall either be punishment
(which will herald the beginning of their punishment in the Aakhirah).
will know who has the worst standing and who has the weakest army.”
v.s: Say, "Whoever is in error - let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension [in wealth and time] until, when they see that which they were promised - either punishment [in this world] or the Hour [of resurrection] - they will come to know who is worst in position and weaker in soldiers."
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Whoever is ˹entrenched˺ in misguidance, the Most Compassionate will allow them plenty of time, until—behold!—they face what they are threatened with: either the torment or the Hour. Only then will they realize who is worse in position and inferior in manpower.”

q: of those who are rightly guided

(all good acts in general, but especially those acts benefit and rewards of which continue after the death of the doer, such as digging a well or borehole from which people continue to get water even after the sponsor's death)
are best in the sight of your Rabb in terms of reward and best in terms of consequences
v.s: And God increases those who were guided, in guidance, and the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward and better for recourse.
v.c: And Allah increases in guidance those who are ˹rightly˺ guided. And the everlasting good deeds are far better with your Lord in reward and in outcome.

q: Have you seen him who rejects Our Aayaat and says, “I shall certainly be granted
(in the Aakhirah just as I have them in this world).”
v.s: Then, have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children [in the next life]"?
v.c: Have you seen ˹O Prophet˺ the one who rejects Our revelations yet boasts, “I will definitely be granted ˹plenty of˺ wealth and children ˹if there is an afterlife˺.”?

q: Has he peeked into the unseen or has he made a pact with Ar Rahmaan
(because of which he seems so convinced.)?
v.s: Has he looked into the unseen, or has he taken from the Most Merciful a promise?
v.c: Has he looked into the unseen or taken a pledge from the Most Compassionate?

q: Never! We shall shortly record what he says and continue
to intensify the punishment for him
v.s: No! We will record what he says and extend [i.e., increase] for him from the punishment extensively.
v.c: Not at all! We certainly record whatever he claims and will increase his punishment extensively.

m: and he will come to Us
q: about and he will come to Us all alone
v.s: And We will inherit him [in] what he mentions, and he will come to Us alone.
v.c: And We will inherit what he boasts of, and he will come before Us all by himself.

q: so that these may be a means of strength for them
(they believe that these Aaliha will be able to intercede for them before Allaah).
v.s: And they have taken besides God [false] deities that they would be for them [a source of] honour.
v.c: They have taken other gods, instead of Allah, seeking strength ˹and protection˺ through them.
v.h: Believers and Disbelievers on Judgment Day

q: (will claim that the Mushrikeen never worshipped them)

(Idols will deny being worshipped because being lifeless, they had no idea that they were worshipped. As for living beings who were regarded as gods, they will deny being worshipped because the object of worship is to please the one being worshipped and instead of pleasing the ones being worshipped, the worshippers will have caused more problems for them, especially in the Aakhirah. Therefore, since the object of worship is lost, it is as if no worship took place at all. See also verse 28 of Surah 10 and verse 86 of Surah 16.)
v.s: No! They [i.e., those "gods"] will deny their worship of them and will be against them opponents [on the Day of Judgement].
v.c: But no! Those ˹gods˺ will deny their worship and turn against them.

q: Have you not seen that We have set
v.s: Do you not see that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them [to evil] with [constant] incitement?
v.c: Do you ˹O Prophet˺ not see that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers, constantly inciting them?

q: (by asking Allaah to send His punishment)
We are meticulously keeping records of them
(and they will be taken to task for everything they did when the time arrives).
v.s: So be not impatient over them. We only count out [i.e., allow] to them a [limited] number.
v.c: So do not be in haste against them, for indeed We are ˹closely˺ counting down their days.

q: when We shall gather those with Taqwa unto Ar Rahmaan as
v.s: On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation
v.c: ˹Watch for˺ the Day We will gather the righteous before the Most Compassionate as an honoured delegation,

q: And We will drag the criminals
v.s: And will drive the criminals to Hell in thirst
v.c: and drive the wicked to Hell like a thirsty herd.

q: from Ar Rahmaan will have the ability to intercede
v.s: None will have [power of] intercession except he who had taken from the Most Merciful a covenant.
v.c: None will have the right to intercede, except those who have taken a covenant from the Most Compassionate.

q: say, “Ar Rahmaan has taken a child.”
v.s: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken [for Himself] a son."
v.c: They say, “The Most Compassionate has offspring.”

q: You have certainly said a grave thing.
v.s: You have done an atrocious thing.
v.c: You have certainly made an outrageous claim,

q: The heavens may split asunder because of it, the earth may be cleaved open and the mountains may crash to pieces.
v.s: The heavens almost rupture therefrom and the earth splits open and the mountains collapse in devastation
v.c: by which the heavens are about to burst, the earth to split apart, and the mountains to crumble to pieces

q: Because they ascribed children to Ar Rahmaan.
v.s: That they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.
v.c: in protest of attributing children to the Most Compassionate.

q: It is not befitting of Ar Rahmaan to take children
(because He has no need for children when everything belongs to Him).
v.s: And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful that He should take a son.
v.c: It does not befit ˹the majesty of˺ the Most Compassionate to have children.

q: (On the Day of Qiyaamah and in this world)
Everything within the heavens and the earth shall come to Ar Rahmaan as slaves
v.s: There is no one in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant.
v.c: There is none in the heavens or the earth who will not return to the Most Compassionate in full submission.

q: Allaah has counted them all and numbered them all precisely
(therefore, none of them can ever hide from Him and absent himself or herself on the Day of Qiyaamah).
v.s: He has enumerated them and counted them a [full] counting.
v.c: Indeed, He fully knows them and has counted them precisely.

q: Each one of them will come to Him all alone on the Day of Qiyaamah
(without any wealth to offer as ransom and without any friend, assistant or lawyer to save him from punishment).
v.s: And all of them are coming to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.
v.c: And each of them will return to Him on the Day of Judgment all alone.

q: As for those who have Imaan and do good acts, Ar Rahmaan will soon authorise
(Allaah guides them to perform good deeds and to possess excellent conduct because of which He loves them and the people love them and speak favourably about them.)
v.s: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.
v.c: As for those who believe and do good, the Most Compassionate will ˹certainly˺ bless them with ˹genuine˺ love.

m: that you may give glad tidings
q: We have made the Qur'aan easy
on your tongue so that with it you may convey
to those with Taqwa and warn the quarrelsome people
(that they will be punished if they do not stop arguing about the fundamental aspects of islaam).
v.s: So, [O Muhammad], We have only made it [i.e., the Qur’ān] easy in your tongue [i.e., the Arabic language] that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a hostile people.
v.c: Indeed, We have made this ˹Quran˺ easy in your own language ˹O Prophet˺ so with it you may give good news to the righteous and warn those who are contentious.

q: How many were the generations that We destroyed before them
(who also refused to give up their quarrels)!
Do you see any of them or do you hear any whisper
(They were destroyed so effectively that there remains no trace of them.)
v.s: And how many have We destroyed before them of generations? Do you perceive of them anyone or hear from them a sound?
v.c: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We have destroyed before them! Do you ˹still˺ see any of them, or ˹even˺ hear from them the slightest sound?
